legend: Every flag below is attached to at least one row and is shown on the Flagged for Review page. A flag is not proof of wrongdoing — it marks something a buyer cannot confirm from the seller's own page and must resolve before paying.

flags.label: Weight not published
flags.what: The seller's page does not state the ring's metal weight in grams, so melt value cannot be computed and the price-per-gram test cannot be applied.
flags.why_it_matters: Your checklist requires the weight before purchase. Without it, any price-per-gram figure would be an invention.
flags.action: Ask the seller in writing for the weight in grams (and whether it is gold-only or total item weight). Keep the reply.

flags.label: Hallmark and/or maker's mark not published
flags.what: The page does not describe the stamp inside the band or the manufacturer's mark.
flags.why_it_matters: National Stamping Act (15 U.S.C. 297), summarised in 16 CFR 23.10, requires a quality mark on gold to be accompanied by the maker's trademark or name. A karat stamp with no maker's mark is incomplete.
flags.action: Ask for a close-up photo of the stamp before purchase; verify both the karat and the maker's mark.

flags.label: "18k" in the name, but not solid gold
flags.what: The piece is 18k gold vermeil: a gold layer over a sterling silver base. The seller's own spec says the 18k gold is a plating layer on recycled sterling silver.
flags.why_it_matters: 16 CFR 23.4 defines vermeil as a sterling silver base plated with gold of a stated thickness. A buyer scanning for "18k" could reasonably assume solid gold.
flags.action: Do not treat this as a solid-gold ring. If solid gold is required, exclude it.

flags.label: "Solid" is not stated by the seller
flags.what: The seller states the karat (e.g. 14K / 18K) but never uses the word "solid".
flags.why_it_matters: Your checklist requires the listing to say solid gold explicitly. A karat alone does not rule out hollow construction, plating over base metal, or a two-metal build.
flags.action: Get written confirmation that the item is solid 14k/18k gold throughout, and that it is not hollow.

flags.label: Price is the setting only
flags.what: The figure shown is Blue Nile's "Setting Price". The centre diamond is priced separately, so the delivered ring costs more than the number in this table.
flags.why_it_matters: Comparing a setting price against a complete ring's price is an apples-to-oranges comparison. Any price-per-gram or melt test done on the setting price alone is meaningless.
flags.action: Add a centre stone to the builder and record the all-in total before comparing.

flags.label: Price not displayed on the page
flags.what: The product page as fetched showed no price for this item.
flags.why_it_matters: No price means no comparison is possible, and no price was invented to fill the gap.
flags.action: Check the price while signed in, or at a warehouse, and record it with the date and a screenshot.

flags.label: Return policy excludes precious metals
flags.what: Costco's official return policy lists "Precious metals are non-refundable".
flags.why_it_matters: This conflicts directly with your requirement that you can return the ring after inspecting it. Gold jewellery is a precious metal.
flags.action: Confirm in writing, for this specific item, whether a return is possible before buying. If not, this deal fails your checklist.

flags.label: Very short return window
flags.what: Wilson's requires contact within 7 calendar days of delivery, then the item must be shipped back within 3 calendar days of receiving the return label. Items are sold "as is". Cancelled orders are not refunded the 3% card processing fee.
flags.why_it_matters: An independent jeweller's assay or XRF test usually needs an appointment. A 7-day window can expire before verification is possible — the exact failure mode your checklist warns about.
flags.action: Line up the appraiser before delivery, or negotiate the return window in writing.

flags.label: Bank wire accepted as a payment method
flags.what: Blue Nile's return policy refers to refunds being issued back via bank wire or ACH, which means bank wire is an accepted way to pay.
flags.why_it_matters: Your checklist prefers a credit card for purchase protection and warns against irreversible payment methods. A wire is money you cannot claw back through a chargeback.
flags.action: Pay by credit card even if a wire discount is offered.

flags.label: Engraving voids the return
flags.what: Mejuri and Blue Nile both exclude engraved or personalised items from returns. Mejuri adds that free engraving is optional but makes the item non-returnable.
flags.why_it_matters: A free engraving can quietly convert a returnable ring into a final sale — exactly the exclusion your checklist tells you to look for.
flags.action: Skip engraving until after the ring has been inspected and verified.

flags.label: Large-diamond return is a credit memo, not a refund
flags.what: For diamonds of 1.00 ct or larger, Costco requires all original IGI/GIA paperwork and issues a jewellery credit memo after its own gemologist inspects the stone.
flags.why_it_matters: A credit memo is store credit, not money back. It also assumes you kept the certificate — so documentation retention is part of your return path.
flags.action: Keep every certificate and appraisal with the receipt from day one.

flags.label: Weight includes the stones
flags.what: The published weight is "total weight" of the finished ring, diamonds included. Gold-only weight is lower, so a melt calculation using this number is an upper bound, not the gold content.
flags.why_it_matters: Using total item weight as gold weight systematically overstates melt value — a classic way an otherwise honest calculator produces a wrong number.
flags.action: Ask for the mounting weight excluding stones, or accept that the melt figure is a ceiling.

flags.label: No independent assay or XRF result
flags.what: No seller in this study publishes a per-item XRF scan or an independent assay. The karat is the seller's own statement, backed at most by a stamp.
flags.why_it_matters: Your checklist's key point: a stamp proves nothing by itself. Every row here still needs post-delivery verification by an independent jeweller.
flags.action: Commission XRF or assay on arrival, before wearing or resizing.

flags.label: Unusual karat / not gold throughout
flags.what: This piece is stamped 19 karat — uncommon in the US market — and carries black enamel inlay, so part of the item is not gold.
flags.why_it_matters: 19K is 79.17% gold by definition, but an unusual fineness deserves an assay rather than trust. Enamel also means the item is not gold throughout.
flags.action: Have the fineness assayed; treat the enamel areas as non-gold in any value estimate.

flags.label: Verified at listing level only
flags.what: Price and material were taken from the seller's collection/listing page; the individual product page was not re-fetched in this session.
flags.why_it_matters: Collection pages can lag product pages. The figure is official but less durable.
flags.action: Open the product page and re-confirm price before buying.

flags.label: Product page not individually fetched
flags.what: The row's price comes from Blue Nile's official engagement-ring listing, which displays "Setting Price" next to each item.
flags.why_it_matters: The listing is an official source, but an individual item page is stronger evidence and may carry extra exclusions.
flags.action: Open the item page and re-confirm price, metal and exclusions before buying.

flags.label: Independent review research not completed
flags.what: Independent third-party reviews/complaints were not verified against a primary review source in this session, so no reputation score is asserted.
flags.why_it_matters: Your checklist requires independent review research. Inventing a rating would be a hallucination, so this is left open.
flags.action: Check BBB, Trustpilot and state AG complaint databases before buying.

flags.label: Product page says the item is non-returnable
flags.what: Tiffany & Co.'s own product page for The Tiffany Setting states: "Please note that this item is non returnable" and "this item can only be exchanged".
flags.why_it_matters: Your checklist requires that you can return the ring after inspecting it, including after an independent test. Exchange-only means you cannot get your money back if the assay disappoints.
flags.action: Get the return terms confirmed in writing for the exact configuration before paying. If exchange-only stands, the ring fails your return requirement.

flags.label: Rhodium-plated surface on white gold
flags.what: The listing states a rhodium finish on 14K white gold.
flags.why_it_matters: Rhodium is a surface plating over the gold alloy, not the body metal. 16 CFR 23.7 requires that this surface layer be disclosed, and it wears away with time.
flags.action: Budget for re-plating every few years, or choose yellow gold if you do not want a plated surface.

flags.label: Weight is explicitly approximate
flags.what: The seller publishes a gram weight but qualifies it: "All weights and measurements are approximate".
flags.why_it_matters: An approximate weight still beats no weight, but melt-value maths on it inherits that uncertainty.
flags.action: Treat the melt figure as indicative; ask for the actual weight of the specific piece before shipping.

flags.label: Very light band
flags.what: A published weight under 1 gram for a full ring.
flags.why_it_matters: At this weight there is very little gold, so the melt value is small relative to the asking price, and the band will feel and wear differently from a heavier ring. It is the clearest illustration of why the gram figure matters more than the karat badge.
flags.action: Decide whether you want a ring this light before comparing it on price alone.

flags.label: Two metals in one ring
flags.what: An 18k yellow gold band combined with a platinum head.
flags.why_it_matters: 16 CFR 23.8 requires the relative quantities of precious metals in a multi-metal product to be disclosed and listed in order of weight. "18k gold" alone does not describe this ring's composition.
flags.action: Ask which metal dominates by weight before valuing the gold content.

flags.label: "Starting from" price
flags.what: The price shown is the entry configuration, not a fixed price for the ring pictured.
flags.why_it_matters: The figure varies with the centre stone. Comparing it with a fixed price elsewhere compares two different things.
flags.action: Configure the exact stone you want and record that total, with the date.

flags.label: Availability unclear or unavailable
flags.what: The page showed unavailable or sold-out indicators during verification.
flags.why_it_matters: A price you cannot actually transact at is not a live price.
flags.action: Confirm stock before relying on the price.

flags.label: Price differed between live page and cached copy
flags.what: A search-engine copy of the same URL showed a different figure than the live page.
flags.why_it_matters: This is the exact mechanism by which a hallucinated price enters a project like this. The live page wins; the stale figure is recorded only so the discrepancy stays visible.
flags.action: Always read the live page, never a cached snippet.

flags.label: Listing is dead or redirects
flags.what: The product URL now 404s, is sold out, or redirects to a different retailer.
flags.why_it_matters: Dead listings are excluded from the price table rather than quoted from a stale copy.
flags.action: None — recorded for completeness.

flags.label: Return policy page not read
flags.what: No official return-policy page was captured for this seller, so return terms are unknown rather than favourable. As of the P3 pass on 2026-10-22 this applies only to James Allen, whose product URLs redirect to Blue Nile; Ross-Simons and Catbird had their policy pages read and now carry sourced terms.
flags.why_it_matters: An unread policy is not a permissive one. Assuming a return right that has not been verified is how buyers get stuck.
flags.action: Read the seller's return policy before ordering and keep a copy.

flags.label: Seller page contradicts itself on metal/karat
flags.what: The listing title and spec table say 18K White Gold, while the same page's product description says the ring is "crafted from warmly lustrous 14k yellow gold".
flags.why_it_matters: If the seller's own page cannot agree with itself about the metal, the karat stamp is the only thing left to trust — and that is exactly what your checklist says not to rely on alone.
flags.action: Ask the seller in writing which alloy the ring is made in and get the answer on the product page or by email. Have the metal tested (XRF) on arrival before accepting it.

flags.label: Product URL redirects to a different product path
flags.what: The linked Tiffany URL redirects to a different product path (/jewelry/rings/18k-rose-gold-and-platinum-diamond-rings-1712.html). The page served there still shows The Tiffany Setting in 18k yellow gold, so the facts were verified, but the link is not stable.
flags.why_it_matters: A redirect can silently land a buyer on a different product later. A dead or drifting link is how a stale price becomes an invented one.
flags.action: Re-open the link before buying and confirm the title, price and metal on the page you land on.

flags.label: Identifier on the page differs from the identifier in the URL
flags.what: The Costco URL ends in /100675127, while the page that loads shows "Item 1596365". The product title matched, so the row is kept, but the two identifiers disagree.
flags.why_it_matters: If you quote an item number to Costco or to a card issuer in a dispute, the wrong one can void your complaint trail.
flags.action: Use the item number printed on the page (1596365) and keep a dated screenshot of it next to the URL.

flags.label: Published weight is explicitly approximate
flags.what: The seller publishes a gram weight but qualifies it. Sarraf states an accuracy of ± 5%; Ross-Simons states that all weights and measurements are approximate.
flags.why_it_matters: A tolerance turns a precise-looking melt calculation into a range. Presenting the midpoint as fact would overstate the precision of the number.
flags.action: Treat any melt figure from this weight as an estimate within the seller's stated tolerance, and confirm the actual weight on a jeweller's scale after delivery.

flags.label: Weight published for a reference size, not the size you order
flags.what: Sarraf states: "The weight listed is an approximate weight of a ring in size 10". The ring is sold in sizes 3 to 16.
flags.why_it_matters: Metal weight changes with ring size. Using the size-10 figure for a size 5 ring overstates its gold content.
flags.action: Ask for the weight of the exact size you intend to buy, or weigh the delivered ring before arguing about value.

flags.label: One weight covers more than one metal option
flags.what: Automic Gold states "Approximately 5.4g for gold or 8.1g for platinum" — one line covering two metals with different densities.
flags.why_it_matters: If you order the platinum version, the gold figure is the wrong number, and vice versa. A single value read out of context becomes a false claim.
flags.action: Quote the metal alongside the weight whenever you rely on it, and check the delivered ring's weight.

flags.label: Return window exists but is conditional and short-fused
flags.what: Sarraf accepts returns within 30 days of receipt, but only in original condition: "Items that show signs of wear or have been resized (by a jeweler other than Sarraf Jewelry Inc.), altered, special ordered items or damaged in any way cannot be accepted for return", and "Orders which are over 30 days of receipt do not qualify for return policy." "Engraving and shipping Charges are nonrefundable" — an engraved ring may still be returned, exchanged or resized where possible (special orders excepted), but "the $25.00 engraving fee is non-refundable".
flags.why_it_matters: A return right you cannot practically use is not protection. Waiting past the window, or wearing the ring once, can end it.
flags.action: Inspect on arrival, keep the packaging untouched, and start the return in writing inside the window if anything fails verification.
flags.correction_note: P3 correction, 2026-10-22 (session arena/699d8e05-gold3): this entry previously said "A cancelled order is charged a 3% card-processing fee (Wilson's terms state the same fee structure)". Sarraf's return policy was re-read end to end on the live page and contains no such fee — the 3% cancellation fee is Wilson's ("orders cancelled prior to shipment will not be refunded for credit card processing fees incurred at the rate of 3%", wilsonsestatejewelry.com). The fees Sarraf does publish are the $25.00 engraving fee and, for warranty repair or replacement, "a Shipping and handling fee of $100.00 or 10% of purchase price which ever amount is greater" (see WAR1). A number belonging to one seller had been attached to another — the exact failure mode this board exists to catch.

flags.label: Engraving makes the item final sale
flags.what: The product page states that engraved items are final sale, and engraving is offered as an option at checkout.
flags.why_it_matters: A free or cheap engraving can quietly remove the return right that the rest of the policy advertises.
flags.action: Decline engraving until the ring has been independently verified, or accept that the purchase becomes non-returnable.

flags.label: A fee is deducted from the refund
flags.what: Ross-Simons charges "a flat fee of $4.95 for return shipping and handling"; Catbird states "An $9 charge for return shipping will be deducted from your refund" and that "All international sales are final."
flags.why_it_matters: A return right that costs money is still a real right, but the fee is only visible in the policy text, not in the "free returns" headline. On a low-value band it is a meaningful share of the refund.
flags.action: Read the fee before you order, and factor it into the decision to buy two sizes to compare.

flags.label: Resizing or altering the ring ends the return right
flags.what: Ross-Simons: "Merchandise that has been damaged, altered, or resized by a jeweler other than Ross-Simons cannot be accepted for return." Sarraf: items "resized (by a jeweler other than Sarraf Jewelry Inc.), altered, special ordered items or damaged in any way cannot be accepted for return". Blue Nile excludes "items resized after initial purchase".
flags.why_it_matters: Your checklist has the ring sized, inspected and possibly XRF-tested by an independent jeweller on arrival. If that jeweller resizes it first, these sellers stop accepting the return — the verification step has to happen before any work is done on the ring.
flags.action: Inspect and test first, resize second. If a resize is needed, ask the seller to do it (Blue Nile offers one free resize within two sizes in 6 months; Sarraf offers lifetime refinishing) so the return right survives.

flags.label: The warranty costs money to use
flags.what: Sarraf's lifetime guarantee covers defects in materials and workmanship, but "All jewelry returned for repair or replacement are subject to a Shipping and handling fee of $100.00 or 10% of purchase price which ever amount is greater", must be accompanied by the original invoice, excludes chipped or missing stones and normal wear and tear, and "Third Party alteration to the jewelry will automatically void the Lifetime Guarantee". The policy also ends with "Sarraf reserves the right to modify this policy at any time and without notice".
flags.why_it_matters: A lifetime guarantee that charges $100 or 10% per visit — and that a third-party resize voids outright — is not the protection the headline implies.
flags.action: Price the warranty before relying on it, keep every invoice, and use only the seller's own service if you want the guarantee to survive.

flags.label: One page states the same term two different ways
flags.what: Automic Gold's product page says "Production time is 4-8 business days" in the buy box and "This item is made to order. Production time is 1-2 weeks. If you are adding engraving, production time is 2-3 weeks." in its Shipping & Returns section. Aurate's solitaire page describes "a refined 1.8mm width" in the copy while its specs block lists "Width: 2.75mm" and "Thickness: 1.8mm".
flags.why_it_matters: When a page disagrees with itself, neither sentence can be quoted as the fact. Recording both, verbatim, is the only honest option — picking one would be an invention dressed as a citation.
flags.action: Ask the seller to confirm the term (lead time, width, weight) in writing before ordering, and keep the reply with the order.
